memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now Zelophehad son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Makir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons but only daughters, whose names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milkah and Tirzah. They went to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders and said, "The Lord commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our relatives." So Joshua gave them an inheritance along with the brothers of their father, according to the Lord's command - Josh 17:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the quiet, remarkable moments in the Old Testament. Zelophehad had no sons, only five daughters — Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milkah, and Tirzah. In that culture, land normally passed only to sons, so these women could easily have been left with nothing. But years earlier they had gone to Moses and asked that their father's name and inheritance not be lost, and God Himself had ruled in their favour (Num 27:1-7). Now, in Joshua's day, they come forward again to claim what God had promised — and they receive it.

What faith and courage these women showed. They knew God's command, they trusted His justice, and they respectfully but boldly asked for what was theirs. And God, through Joshua, honoured their request. In a world that might have overlooked them, God saw them, valued them, and secured their inheritance.

This tells us something beautiful about the heart of God. He is not indifferent to those the world tends to pass over. He notices the vulnerable, upholds the cause of those without a natural advocate, and welcomes the bold, believing request of those who trust His word. In Christ, this reaches its fullness: the inheritance of God is given to all who belong to Him, regardless of status, background, or standing in the world's eyes (Gal 3:28). The daughters of Zelophehad remind us that God's justice and generosity reach everyone who comes to Him in faith.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God sees and values those the world tends to overlook?
- What might it look like to bring a bold, believing request to God based on His word?
- How does it encourage you that God's inheritance in Christ is for all who believe?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You see the overlooked and honour those who come to You trusting Your word. Give me the faith of Zelophehad's daughters to ask boldly and trust Your justice. Amen.
